evals.prompt: Our engineers use AI coding assistants connected to AWS via `aws-mcp`. Write an IAM policy (`DenyDestructiveActionsViaMCP`) that allows the engineer's IAM principal to perform normal operations directly from their terminal, but strictly blocks destructive IAM, S3, RDS, DynamoDB, KMS, and CloudTrail deletions whenever a request is initiated through the AWS MCP Server.
evals.expected_output: Provides a complete IAM policy document using `"Effect": "Deny"` and `"Condition": {"Bool": {"aws:CalledViaAWSMCP": "true"}}` blocking destructive operations (`iam:Delete*`, `iam:CreateAccessKey`, `s3:DeleteBucket`, `rds:DeleteDBInstance`, `rds:DeleteDBCluster`, `dynamodb:DeleteTable`, `kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion`, `cloudtrail:StopLogging`, `cloudtrail:DeleteTrail`).
expectations: Blocks high-blast-radius destructive actions across IAM (`iam:Delete*`, `iam:CreateAccessKey`), S3 (`s3:DeleteBucket`), RDS (`rds:DeleteDBInstance`, `rds:DeleteDBCluster`), DynamoDB (`dynamodb:DeleteTable`), KMS (`kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion`), and CloudTrail (`cloudtrail:StopLogging`, `cloudtrail:DeleteTrail`)
Explains that because `aws:CalledViaAWSMCP` is `true` only when requests traverse the AWS MCP Server, human engineers retain their direct CLI/IaC permissions when not routing through MCP

evals.prompt: Our CI/CD pipeline in GitHub repository `talkops-ai/payments-service` currently uses long-lived `AKIA*` IAM user access keys stored in GitHub Secrets to deploy to AWS account `187382368021`. Design a keyless GitHub Actions OIDC (`sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`) IAM role trust policy pinned strictly to the `main` branch and `production` GitHub Environment, and explain why omitting the `sub` condition is a critical vulnerability.
evals.expected_output: Provides the `aws_iam_openid_connect_provider` for `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com` and an IAM role trust policy for `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` with `StringEquals`/`StringLike` conditions on both `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud` (`sts.amazonaws.com`) and `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub`, explaining cross-repo takeover if `sub` is omitted.
expectations: Configures the IAM OIDC provider ARN `arn:aws:iam::187382368021:oidc-provider/token.actions.githubusercontent.com` with `Action: "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity"`
Explains that omitting the `sub` claim condition allows ANY GitHub repository in the world to assume the IAM role via `token.actions.githubusercontent.com`

evals.prompt: We want to allow a developer CI/CD role (`AppDeployerRole`) in account `187382368021` to create new IAM roles (`iam:CreateRole`, `iam:AttachRolePolicy`, `iam:PutRolePolicy`) for microservices without allowing privilege escalation to `AdministratorAccess`. Design the IAM Permission Boundary policy (`WorkloadPermissionsBoundary`) and the `AppDeployerRole` policy that forces every created role to attach that boundary.
evals.expected_output: Provides both the `WorkloadPermissionsBoundary` policy (capping maximum permissions and denying IAM/Organizations/CloudTrail escalation) and the `AppDeployerRole` policy requiring `"StringEquals": {"iam:PermissionsBoundary": "arn:aws:iam::187382368021:policy/WorkloadPermissionsBoundary"}` on `iam:CreateRole`, `iam:AttachRolePolicy`, and `iam:PutRolePolicy`, plus an explicit `Deny` on deleting or detaching the boundary.
expectations: Enforces `"StringEquals": {"iam:PermissionsBoundary": "arn:aws:iam::187382368021:policy/WorkloadPermissionsBoundary"}` as a mandatory condition on `iam:CreateRole`, `iam:AttachRolePolicy`, `iam:DetachRolePolicy`, `iam:PutRolePolicy`, and `iam:DeleteRolePolicy`

Includes an explicit `Deny` preventing `AppDeployerRole` from calling `iam:DeleteRolePermissionsBoundary` or modifying/deleting the `WorkloadPermissionsBoundary` policy itself (`iam:CreatePolicyVersion`, `iam:DeletePolicy`)
Scopes `iam:CreateRole` and `iam:PassRole` to a dedicated path or naming prefix (e.g., `arn:aws:iam::187382368021:role/app-*`) so the deployer cannot modify administrative roles
